sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:10

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:10:1
items.html:
There is here in the words of the Rav a very deep and important matter, for this is the secret of the second Tzimtzum that occurred in the Netzach-Hod-Yesod of Adam Kadmon, brought in the words of the Rav (in Etz Chaim, Gate 8, Chapter 2), that this matter of the second Tzimtzum is the secret of the joining of the attribute of mercy with judgment, as our Sages said; and a thorough understanding of the matter can be found in my book (Panim Meirot uMasbirot, Branch 15, see there), and here we shall be brief. The matter is that only phase four of the aforementioned four phases is called the attribute of judgment, because upon it was the first Tzimtzum, as above in the previous lessons, whereas in the first three phases there was no Tzimtzum at all, and they are therefore called attributes of mercy. However, in the second Tzimtzum of Adam Kadmon, a joining and union of phase four with phase two was made with one another, in the secret of the verse "and the two of them went" — for Malchut and Za rose to Bina, and thus the attribute of judgment, which is phase four, is found sweetened in the attribute of mercy, which is phase two. In such a way that in the first Tzimtzum only phase four alone was restricted, while in the second Tzimtzum Bina too was restricted, on account of its joining with Malchut, as stated. And this matter took place in the Netzach-Hod-Yesod of Adam Kadmon from its navel downward; and therefore these ten Sefirot, which emerged joined with the attribute of judgment, are called by the name World of Points, after the ascent of Malchut which is called a point.
And thus it is discerned that in the aforementioned World of Points, Za and Malchut separated from the four phases Hochma-Bina, Tiferet-Malchut; for since phase four ascended to the place of Bina and became a screen there, the upper light was cut off at the Malchut within Bina and did not expand to Za, which is called garment, or to Malchut, which is called sanctuary, since they are found below Bina.
And this is what the Rav writes: "Know that the root, the souls, and the bodies are one phase between which there is no separation, but the garments and sanctuaries are two phases separated from the three aforementioned phases," end of quote. And this is as stated — that because of the screen fixed at the bottom of Bina, the light is cut off there, and from there onward, in all the worlds, no upper light reaches the interiority of these instances of Za and Malchut, and therefore they became, for this reason, phases of encompassing vessels, meaning that they receive the light from a distance, since the upper light no longer clothes within them. And the garment is a vessel for the light of Chaya, and the sanctuary is a vessel for the light of Yechida.
And from what has been said you will understand that those instances of Za and Malchut found within the four phases, in all the worlds from the World of Points downward, are regarded as the Za and Malchut particular to Bina, and therefore the upper light clothes within their interiority as well. However, those general instances of Za and Malchut, namely those found below Bina, are separated from the inner vessels in which Neshama, Ruach, and Nefesh of Ohr Pnimi clothe, and became encompassing vessels of Chaya and Yechida.

items.html: This matter has been explained well and at length in Inner Observation (Part 2, Chapter 1, item 7), and with what is explained there you will be able to understand for yourself the whole continuation of the Rav's words, and there is no need to elaborate further.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:10:3
items.html: Neshamot are the phase of the World of Beriah. Ruchin are the phase of the World of Yetzirah. Nefashot are the phase of the World of Assiya. And this is what the Rav writes: "from the World of Atzilut, Neshamot" — meaning, Neshamot that are in Beriah are drawn from the World of Atzilut to Beriah. "And from Beriah, Ruchin" — meaning, the Ruchin that are in Yetzirah are drawn there from the World of Beriah. For from the coupling of Zeir Anpin and Nukva of Atzilut, Neshamot are drawn to the righteous who stand in Beriah; and from the coupling of Zeir Anpin and Nukva of Beriah, Ruchin are drawn to those who stand in Yetzirah.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:10:4
items.html:
This is the rule: the Nefesh of a degree is considered, for the degree below it, to be the phase of Ruach. And the Ruach of the upper one is considered, for the lower one, to be the phase of Neshama. And the Neshama of the upper one is Chaya to the lower one. And the Chaya of the upper one is considered Yechida to the lower one.
And accordingly you will understand that the Nefesh of Ruach is considered Ruach for the degree of Nefesh; and the Ruach of Ruach is considered Neshama for the degree of Nefesh, and so on in this manner. Therefore, what the Rav writes — "that sometimes there will be one who has only the degree of Nefesh, and he is more important than one who has Ruach" — he means that one who has the Neshama of Nefesh is more important than one who has the Nefesh of Ruach. This is because the Neshama of Nefesh is equal in weight to the Ruach of Ruach, as above, yet more important than the Nefesh of Ruach.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:10:5
items.html: There are four spellings of the Name Yud-Hei-Vav-Hei. First: the spelling of Yudin, Yud Hei Yud Vav Yud Hei, whose numerical value is 72 (Ayin-Bet). Second: the spelling of Yudin and Alef, Yud Hei Yud Vav Alef Hei, whose numerical value is 63 (Samech-Gimel). Third: the spelling of Alfin, Yud Hei Alef Vav Alef Hei, whose numerical value is 45 (Mem-Hei). Fourth: the spelling of Hein, whose numerical value is 52 (Bet-Nun). And the spelling of 72 alludes to Chochma, which is the letter Yud of the Name. And the spelling of 63 alludes to Bina, which is the letter Hei of the Name. And the spelling of 45 alludes to Zeir Anpin, which is the letter Vav of the Name. And the spelling of 52 alludes to Malchut, which is the final Hei of the Name.
